Figure 1:SO-101 Bench at a glance.(a) Real SO-101 and its digital twin. (b) The four tasks. (c) Sim2real:
five policies trained without real data keep their ranking on the real robot. (d) Leaderboard. (e) Harness
ablation. (f) The language model matters.

Figure 2:The four SO-101 Bench tasks.Bin, next-to, between and directional move, with the
target paths overlaid on successful simulation episodes. The task panels repeat Fig.1b.

Figure 3:Simulation objectsby generalization split. Orange dots mark physical objects that are also
used in the real-robot evaluation. The 37 private unseen-class objects are held out
to prevent test-set leakage and are not shown.

Figure 4:PLAN and MEM examples(start, middle and end of successful primary-evaluation episodes).
Left: GPT-6.1 Sol with PyRUA-Lean and Galaxea 0.5 rotates the toy boat to fit between the pill planner
and the camera (episode 529), which all nine learned policies fail.
Right: ImageWAM moves the tape backwards (episode 300), retaining the boundary object
position while it is occluded during the move; four of the nine learned policies solve this episode.
All objects and backgrounds shown are public.

Figure 5:Sim–real correspondence of independently trained GR00T N1.6 policies.(a) Success of a
real-only policy on the physical SO-101 and a sim-only policy in the digital twin, per task and object split
(95% Wilson intervals). (b) Composition of hand-annotated failures (next to, between, move): both domains shift
from placement to semantic and grasping failures as object novelty increases. (c) Objects binned in 4-object
bin episodes, real vs. simulation (56 paired episodes; outlined cells are exact agreement).
Below: overhead views of independently trained NVIDIA GR00T N1.6-3B policies executing the same
instruction with the same objects (real trial 52, matched task row 466). Poses and frame times differ.

Figure 6:Sim2real.(a) Policy-level success on the real robot (unseen environment) vs. simulation
(many environments) on the same 45 layouts: the ranking of all five policies is preserved exactly (Spearmanρ=1.00\rho=1.00, MMRV=0.000=0.000) and every policy scores higher in simulation. Diamond: the LLM agent; circles: learned
policies fine-tuned only on simulated demonstrations. (b) Success in simulation and on the real robot per
policy, overall (45 episodes) and per task family (9 episodes), with 95% Wilson intervals.
Bottom: the agent on matched trial 41, a between episode with unseen-class objects that none of the four learned
policies solved on the real robot. Galaxea 0.5 grasps the tongs, then the agent carries and places them, in both domains.

Figure 8:Episodes solved only by GPT-6.1 Sol + PyRUA-Lean v9.6 + Galaxea 0.5.Initial overhead views, cropped to the task workspace, with the exact instructions.
All ten other leaderboard entries failed each episode. Episodes 174 and 471 belong to PLAN.
